summary.intent: Start the planned work lanes from NEXT-WORK.md: fix W2 (SYS-RETRY, rerun after a failed tag push), add the W1 mixed-routing apply test, and begin the W0 docs cleanup.
summary.outcome: PR #202 (W2 fix, just ci passing at 91.59% line coverage) and PR #203 (W1 test-only, just ci passing at 92.40% region coverage) were opened. W0 docs fixes to the W2 worktree were being committed when the session ended, with a final just ci check not yet confirmed.

repo: Release rerun selection previously treated a tag on HEAD as released. The fix observes all operations (registry, tag, GitHub release) for packages tagged at HEAD and keeps them selected until all are satisfied. A tag on an older commit still settles the version without contacting any provider.

The release e2e harness fakes gh, cargo and registry reads, so real provider reads are not proven by the tests. The harness log now records read-only calls, so no-op assertions must compare mutating calls only.
Three existing tests (init preview and two in release/local.rs) assumed a tag on HEAD means released, which was the defect. They now tag an older commit.
just ci gates on coverage (90% threshold) and includes a docs-check recipe. The true result is the log's own exit= line, not the background task notification.
Releases and changesets: a behavior fix to callisto-cli needs a patch changeset, while test-only PRs (W1) need none. AGENTS.md says not to include a session link in commits or PRs.

Docs that restate the retry gap must be updated together: docs/specs/release.json (REL-CMD-01, REL-CMD-08, REL-RERUN-02), docs/architecture/release.md, docs/adr/0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md, and the SYS-RETRY row in docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md.

The W1 mixed-routing test passed on the first run, so it was validated by mutation: dropping the persist in the mixed workspace rewrite step and reordering mixed rewrites ahead of mixed versions were both caught.

code.finding: Roster derivation now takes a 'resumable' set so packages already tagged at HEAD stay selected until every operation is satisfied.
Added an observation helper used by the local plan to observe releases already tagged at HEAD before deciding.
The local plan observes already-tagged releases before deciding. A preview with no origin push URL cannot observe and keeps the old behavior.
Added a mixed-routing apply test with a plain manifest, a resolver-only workspace root and a root that is both package and workspace, asserting exact bytes.

workflow: Write the failing reproduction first. The W2 black-box test failed on the old code with 'Nothing to release.' before the fix.
When a new test passes immediately, prove it can fail with targeted mutations of the source, then revert them and confirm only the test file changed.
Use a separate worktree per work item, and note that the sandbox only permits edits inside the current worktree, so you must exit and re-enter a worktree to edit another.
Check the CI log's exit= line rather than trusting the background-task completion notice.
Check rendered PR bodies after creation, since backslash-escaped backticks in a quoted heredoc stay literal.

friction: The sandbox rejected inline env commands, heredocs, and inline scripts that mention git, forcing workarounds with script files and the Edit tool.
macOS sed rejected a one-liner for editing imports.
The first PR body for #202 had literal backslashes from escaped backticks and needed a follow-up fix.
The first just ci run failed with exit=100 on tests that assumed a tag on HEAD means released, and a second round of failures in local.rs needed more test edits.
A docs gap in #202 (architecture/release.md still listing the old behavior as a known gap) was found only after the PR was opened, requiring a switch back to the W2 worktree.
open_items: W0 docs cleanup: verify each register row in the project docs against the code, prune shipped items, and fix references to pruned files. Deleting remote branches needs user confirmation.
Finish committing the doc fixes to #202 after the final just ci check.
W1 real-service credential check needs a user decision on where it runs in CI.
No independent review has been done on #202, which the plan recommends before merging risky changes.
Real gh, cargo and registry reads in the release rerun path are not covered by tests.
